Global Taste Corp - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Taste Corp Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press *1 on your telephone keypad followed by your four-digit conference ID number. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Taste Corp's Q2 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and Mark Donovan, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q2 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on six key areas: overall company performance highlights, e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue, discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, updates on M&A activity and portfolio management, EBITDA margin performance and key factors, and organic revenue growth overall and by region.

First, regarding overall company performance highlights: This was a resilient quarter for Global Taste, demonstrating the strength of our diversified portfolio across beverages, snacks, and convenience foods amid a dynamic macroeconomic environment. Net revenues reached $15.2 billion, up 8% year-over-year, or 6% on an organic basis excluding FX and acquisitions. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of organic growth, outpacing the global F&B industry average of 3-4% as reported by NielsenIQ. Pricing actions contributed 4 points to this growth, reflecting disciplined management of input cost inflation—now easing to mid-single digits from the double-digit peaks in 2023—while volume/mix added 2 points, driven by innovation and everyday low-price strategies in our core brands like TasteWave sodas and CrunchMaster snacks.

On profitability, adjusted operating income rose 11% to $2.8 billion, expanding adjusted operating margin to 18.4%, up 90 basis points year-over-year. This was fueled by gross margin expansion of 220 basis points to 38.2%, thanks to supply chain efficiencies and favorable commodity hedges on staples like sugar, which fell 15% quarter-over-quarter, corn, which stayed stable, and dairy, up only 2% versus the 12% we had feared. Adjusted EBITDA hit $3.1 billion, a 12% increase, with a margin of 20.4%. Diluted adjusted EPS came in at $1.85, up 12% year-over-year and 5% excluding currency, beating our guidance midpoint and supporting our full-year outlook of $7.40 to $7.60.

In beverages, which make up 52% of revenues, we delivered 9% organic growth to $7.9 billion, led by a 15% surge in functional beverages like our HydroBoost electrolyte line, capitalizing on the $25 billion global hydration market growing at 7% CAGR per Euromonitor. Carbonated soft drinks volumes were flat but pricing rose 6%, mirroring peers like Coca-Cola as consumers traded down to value packs. Hydration and premium non-alcoholic segments offset a 2% dip in juices due to orange concentrate volatility.

Snacks and convenience, 35% of revenues, rose 7% organically to $5.3 billion, with salty snacks like our rebranded ZestChips growing 12% on premium flavors such as sriracha-lime air-fried variants. This taps into the $200 billion global savory snacks market, where health halo products are gaining 10% share. Candy confectionery faced 3% headwinds from cocoa prices spiking 40% year-to-date to $10,000 per ton, but we mitigated via swaps covering 70% of our fiscal 2024 needs.

Dairy and nutritionals, 13% of revenues, grew 5% to $2.0 billion, propelled by plant-based dairy alternatives up 20%, aligning with the 12% CAGR in the $30 billion alt-dairy space according to Innova Market Insights. Our NutriBlend yogurt pods benefited from e-commerce penetration rising to 18% of sales.

Regionally, North America at 60% of revenues saw stellar 10% organic growth to $9.1 billion, with market share gains of 50 basis points in snacks per IRI data, outpacing Frito-Lay and Mondelez. Consumer resilience in mass channels, up 8%, offset club slowdowns. Europe, 20%, had modest 3% growth to $3.0 billion amid regulatory pressures like the UK's HFSS advertising ban and EU front-of-pack labeling, but premium ice cream lines grew 9%. We're adapting with reformulations reducing sugar by 15% across 40 SKUs. Asia-Pacific and Latin America, 20%, showed robust 12% organic growth to $3.1 billion, driven by Indonesia and Brazil expansions—such as TasteWave CSD launches capturing 2% market share in a 5% growing market. China hydration volumes rose 18%, though inflation hedging was key against rice syrup costs.

Strategically, we're executing on innovation, portfolio optimization, and sustainability. We launched 25 new products, including AI-optimized formulations via our TasteLab platform—leveraging machine learning to predict consumer preferences with 85% accuracy, reducing R&D cycle time by 30%. This positions us for the $500 billion health and wellness F&B wave. Portfolio-wise, we divested two underperforming legacy dairy assets for $450 million, sharpening focus on high-margin categories with over 15% ROIC. Sustainability includes 45% of agricultural sourcing now regenerative, up from 30% year-over-year, partnering with farmers on soy and wheat via our FarmForward program—cutting Scope 3 emissions 12% and appealing to Gen Z, who drive 25% of premium sales. Water usage per liter of beverage is down 18%, ahead of PepsiCo's targets. Looking ahead, Q3 organic growth guidance is 5-7%, with full-year revenue growth of 6-8% and adjusted EPS growth of 9-11%. We're well-positioned with $4.2 billion in liquidity and capex at 4% of sales focused on automation.

Second, concerning e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue: E-commerce is one of our brightest growth engines, reshaping the competitive landscape in Food & Beverage where traditional channels still dominate at about 85% of volumes globally. In Q2, e-commerce sales reached $2.3 billion, up a robust 48% year-over-year and 12% sequentially, now representing 15.4% of our total quarterly revenue, expanding from 10.2% last year and 8% two years ago. This outpaces the broader F&B e-commerce market's 25-30% growth per Nielsen, driven by inflation-weary consumers seeking value through bulk buys and subscriptions.

Direct-to-consumer via our site, powered by Shopify Plus with Klaviyo marketing automation, contributed 42% at nearly $1 billion, up 62% year-over-year. Average order value hit $52, up 14%, fueled by personalized bundling like 'Pantry Hero' subscription boxes pairing protein shakes with organic trail mix, which grew subscribers 35% to 450,000. Customer acquisition costs improved 18% to $22, with lifetime value at $420 for a 19:1 ratio, thanks to retargeting via Google Performance Max and TikTok Shop.

Marketplaces drove 58%, with Amazon Fresh and Whole Foods online at around $900 million, up 55%, benefiting from FBA-optimized SKUs like single-serve yogurt parfaits in the top 5% of grocery velocity. Instacart and DoorDash added over $500 million, strong in quick-commerce for ReadyMeals, with same-day delivery at 28% in urban markets.

U.S. was 72% at $1.66 billion, up 52%, propelled by cold-chain logistics with UPS Freight. Europe was 18% or $414 million, up 38%, standout in UK via Ocado—PlantPower Energy Drinks saw 2x basket uplift—and Germany through Rewe's app. APAC at 10% or $230 million accelerated 65% via Shopee and Lazada, with live-streaming for Spice Bites generating big promotional weeks. India shows 120% growth on a small base via BigBasket.

Initiatives include an AI-powered recommendation engine on Adobe Sensei and Snowflake, boosting conversions 22% with cross-sells like Keto Bars and Electrolyte Waters. We rationalized to 250 high-margin SKUs, driving e-com gross margins to 42%, 450 basis points above blended average, bypassing distributors. Omnichannel via SAP S/4HANA cut stockouts 35% and lifted BOPIS traffic 15%. Piloting drone delivery with Zipline targets 10% last-mile cost cuts.

E-com informs R&D—2.1 million orders showed 28% uptick in low-sugar functionals, accelerating NutriFresh Zero Cal Hydrate. It added 120 basis points to EBITDA margins. We guide e-com to 18-20% of full-year revenue, scaling to 25% by 2025 with $50 million capex for micro-fulfillment and APAC push, despite parcel rates up 7% and regs like California's DTC labeling.

Third, in terms of discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies: Our pricing actions and RGM strategies were pivotal in delivering 8.2% organic net revenue growth. In F&B, with cocoa up 45% year-to-date, RGM is core, balancing resilience like PepsiCo in snacking or Nestlé in premium coffee.

Pricing drove 5.8 points, up from 4.9% prior quarter, with ASP up 6.2% versus 3.1% CPI. List hikes averaged 7-9% net of promotions. In beverages (52%), 8% hikes on CSDs and juices offset orange concentrate up 25%, NPR 6.5% with EDLP at Walmart limiting elasticity to -0.4x versus category -0.6x. Functionals like VitaEnergy commanded 12% premiums.

Snacks (28%) saw 10% on chocolate amid cocoa peaks, 7% on salty, with 15% trade efficiency via AI, slotting down to 2.3%. Dairy (20%) moderated to 5%, but plant milks hit 11% NPR on innovations.

ML models with NielsenIQ tested 1,200 price-packs, elasticity beverages -0.35x vs. snacks -0.55x. Volume +1.1%, mix +1.3% for total RGM 8.2%, gross margin up 210 bps to 38.4%, offsetting 18% COGS inflation 60% via pricing/mix.

Premiumization shifted 3 points to better-for-you, low-sugar CSDs now 22% volume. Promotions down 5% spend but 10% efficient. North America (55%) 9.5% growth, 6.8% NPR, e-com 14%. EMEA (25%) 7.2%, 5.2% NPR offsetting volume dip. APAC (12%) 10.1%, China +14%. LatAm (8%) 6.8%.

RGM 2.0 integrates SAP Ariba, Palantir, POE simulating 50,000 scenarios at 92% accuracy. Pillars: divested low-RGM brands for $250M, redeployed to plant snacks at 20% CAGR; 25% revenue from new products like collagen yogurts; eco-packaging for 5-7% uplifts. Q4 NPR 5.0-5.5%, RGM 7-9%.

Fourth, looking at updates on M&A activity and portfolio management: M&A and portfolio remain central, focusing on health & wellness, premium snacking, RTD beverages. In Q2, we closed VitalRoots Nutritionals for $425 million net, adding $180 million revenue in plant protein snacks like GreenPulse Bars, 12% CAGR segment. Accretive $0.15 EPS FY24, $35 million synergies: 45% procurement ($16M nuts/oats via Olam), 30% SG&A e-com to 25%, R&D for gut-health.

Pipeline $2.5B dry powder, late-stage in RTD like European kombucha $120M revenue for EU probiotics. Expect Q1 FY25 deal via cash/revolver. Divested canned soup for $280M (9x EBITDA), 4% sales dragging growth 150 bps; proceeds 60% debt to 2.1x leverage, 40% repurchases.

Growth Scorecard AI with Palantir: now 62% revenues high-growth vs. 45% two years ago. Health 28% (+300 bps), premium snacks 22%, RTD 12%. NA (55% $8.2B) bolsters $25B protein market, +120 bps share vs. private label. APAC (20%) tuck-ins plant dairy, Vietnam RTD JV $50M run-rate. Europe (18%) divested chocolate for regs. Sustainability: 100% targets meet Scope 3, VitalRoots 95% regen oats, blockchain with IBM cuts recalls 40%. Organic accelerated to 6.2%, EBITDA +210 bps to 24.5%, ROIC 13.8%, targeting 7-9% EPS CAGR.

Fifth, reviewing EBITDA margin performance and key factors: EBITDA margin hit 18.2%, up 170 basis points from 16.5%, TTM 17.8% upper quartile vs. PepsiCo, General Mills. 'Margin First' amid inflation, Red Sea disruptions, soft demand.

Gross margin +120 bps to 28.4%, mix to premium health SKUs. Snacks (42%) VitaCrunch 35%+ margins vs. 25% legacy, pricing +4.2% (NA 7.5% > CPI 3.2%). Hedging 70% FY24 mitigated dairy/oils +12% QoQ.

SG&A leverage +50 bps to 10.2%, SAP S/4HANA 85% live unlocking $28M savings, ZBB $15M more. Beverages (35%) to 22.1%, PureHydrate +28%. NA (55%) 20.1% +250 bps e-com 18%; EMEA 15.4% offset energy +22%; APAC 14.8%; LatAm 16.2%.

FY23 guide 17.5-18.0%, Q4 mix to 45% premium, ERP/procurement. Regenerative cocoa 200+ farmers, 12-15% premiums for 19%+ FY24 margins.

Sixth, analyzing organic revenue growth overall and by region: Organic revenue growth was 7.2%, accelerating from 5.8%, sixth straight improvement, vs. peers mid-single. 4.1% volume, 2.8% pricing, 0.3% mix; YTD 6.9%, FY midpoint 6-8%. NA 45%, EMEA 25%, APAC 18%, LatAm 10%, ROW 2%.

NA (45%) 9.5%, volumes +5.2%, Quinoa Crunch +18% +120 bps share, Fresha Hydrate +6.8% Walmart doors, e-com 22%. EMEA (25%) 5.1%, +2.9% vol, Fresha Oat Bliss +22% Tesco, +80 bps alt-dairy. APAC (18%) 8.7%, China 12.4% Tmall 35%, Spicy Noodle +30% +150 bps; India 7.9% 20k kiranas. LatAm (10%) 4.8%, Fruit Pops +20%, Guadalajara capex. Premium 42% +500 bps, GLP-1 low-cal +1.5 mix, blockchain +15% certified. RGM AI +150 bps, $200M ag, raising FY24 to 6.5-8.5%.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to provide more detail on our financial results.

John Ramirez (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q2 2024. Net sales were $15.2 billion, representing an 8% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.2%, impacted by supply chain efficiencies and commodity hedges. Operating income was $2.8 billion, and earnings per share were $1.85. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $4.2 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for 6-8% revenue growth and adjusted EPS of $7.40-$7.60.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
If you would like to register a question, please press *1 and your four-digit ID. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

Mike Johnson (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thanks, Mike. Inflation remains a headwind, but our pricing actions and hedging have offset much of it. As I detailed earlier, input costs like cocoa and dairy eased, with hedges covering key commodities—sugar down 15% QoQ, dairy up just 2%. Our RGM delivered 5.8% NPR, outpacing CPI, with elasticity better than peers in inelastic categories like beverages at -0.35x. This protected margins while driving 7.2% organic growth, and we're positioned for moderation ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Carter (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for the new HydroBoost functional beverage and what is the expected impact of the product?

Lisa Chen (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. HydroBoost is expanding rapidly in our hydration portfolio, up 15% this quarter in a $25B market at 7% CAGR. Plans include new AI-optimized flavors via TasteLab, targeting 20% more doors in club and e-com, with subscriptions bundling it for AOV uplift. We expect it to contribute 1-2 points to FY organic growth, accretive to margins at 40%+, leveraging data from 2.1M e-com orders showing strong low-sugar demand.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

David Lee (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Mark Donovan (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, David. We've enhanced resilience through nearshoring like our Guadalajara facility, cutting import reliance 30%, and ERP upgrades reducing stockouts 35%. Hedging covers 70-85% inputs, regenerative sourcing 45% cuts emissions 12%, and blockchain pilots with IBM reduce recalls 40%. Rerouting minimized Ukraine/Red Sea impacts to under 5%, with capex on automation and micro-fulfillment keeping us ahead.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

Rachel Kim (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

John Ramirez (CFO):
Rachel, we're optimistic. Q3 organic 5-7%, full-year revenue 6-8% or 6.5-8.5% raised, EPS growth 9-11% to $7.40-$7.60. Tailwinds from e-com to 18-20%, premium mix to 45%, RGM 7-9%, synergies from VitalRoots. Risks like tariffs hedged, with strong liquidity and balanced portfolio for resilience.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in Global Taste Corp. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
